text:
elaine: Heads-up — I spotted two related Python CVEs during the dependency scan, want a quick triage and patch priority call. Tokenizers wheels have a supply-chain integrity issue (CVE-2026-XXXX) and FastAPI pulls a Starlette path that can lead to header parsing RCE (CVE-2026-YYYY). Poetry lock regen fixes deps but causes macOS wheel failures in CI. Also: KMS audit may require re-encrypting some signing keys, and we should tighten RBAC on who can merge emergency deps PRs. Who can take which piece? :eyes:

sam: I can own tokenizers triage. Quick ask: do we prefer pinning a safe wheel, vendorizing, or backporting a patch? Hosted API customers -> high impact.

dave: For speed I'd pin to the last known-good wheel and add an allowlist in CI while vendorizing in parallel. Example commands to force-lock a version:```
# with poetry
poetry add tokenizers==0.15.1 --lock
# fallback for pip users
pip install "tokenizers==0.15.1"
```
We'll need a changelog entry and a rollout note.

carla: On FastAPI/Starlette: if the patch is in Starlette we may be able to bump only starlette and keep fastapi pinned; but some internal apps rely on FastAPI features that changed between minor versions. Recommend quick compat test in a canary env.

jen-sre: Agree canary. For Redwood Dedicated we should schedule a canary in us-west-2 with traffic-weight 1% for 2 hours. Also RBAC: create a short-lived "deps-emergency" approver group (limit to sec+runtime leads) so only they can merge and trigger production deploys.

maria: KMS note — if we vendorize wheels and sign them with our KMS key, we must record new key usage in audit logs and rotate the signing key after the emergency window. I can coordinate with infra/compliance for a one-time rotation.

elaine: Good. Priority classification suggestion: tokenizers = P0 (hosted inference integrity), fastapi/starlette = P1 (exploit surface smaller but exploitable). Agree?

sam: +1 P0 for tokenizers. I'll open an emergency PR to pin tokenizers and add a CI check. Linking issue when up.

sec-bot: vulndb lookup: CVE-2026-XXXX (tokenizers) — untrusted wheel signature bypass, published 2026-02-12, exploit PoC circulating. CVE-2026-YYYY (starlette header parse) — low reliability but RCE potential, published 2026-02-11.

ci-bot: pipeline red — macos-wheel-build failed on regen-lock branch:```
ERROR: wheel build failed for tokenizers==0.16.0
clang: error: unsupported option '-fno-stack-protector'
```
This is why regen is flaky on macOS runners.

dave: For the macOS failures we should avoid full lock regen as first step. Instead: create focused update PRs per package (tokenizers, starlette) to reduce blast radius. Regen after all patches applied.

carla: Also watch embedding-serving containers — tokenizers pinned could affect quantized wheel compatibility. Requesting runtime bench run after pin.

maria: I'll handle KMS audit with infra; timeline: rotate signing key + publish vendorized wheels in 24-36h post-PR merge. Will create an audit ticket and CC compliance.

elaine: Action items I'm capturing: 1) sam open PR pinning tokenizers + CI allowlist (P0) 2) dave open a vendorize branch and vendorize wheel build 3) carla coordinate canary bump for starlette patch and runtime bench 4) jen-sre create deps-emergency approver RBAC group + canary job 5) maria handle KMS signing and audit ticket. We should aim for initial tokenizers PR within 2 hours.

sam: Opening PR now — will tag @dave for vendor artifacts and @jen-sre for canary. PR title: "emergency: pin tokenizers -> 0.15.1 + ci allowlist". Adding label security/emergency and backport/LTS. :shipit:

ci-bot: PR check started: unit tests running, macos wheels skipped due to allowlist.

dave: I'll start the vendor-build job and push artifacts to our internal package repo. If we sign them with KMS, pass the sig URL in the PR for verification.

jen-sre: RBAC change: I'll open infra PR to add group and update branch protection so only group can merge. Also adding an oncall rotation for emergency merges.

elaine: Thanks all. We'll reconvene in #eng-security in 1h or when PRs are green. If anything blocks, ping me directly. :hammer:

maria: Compliance note: keep all audit logs for 90 days and attach KMS rotation record to the incident folder.

sam: Status update: PR green on CI (unit + integ), macos skip still in effect. Requesting review from sec and runtime.

carla: Quick compatibility result: runtime bench shows negligible perf diff with pinned tokenizers. Proceeding with canary when RBAC group ready.

elaine: Final: merge tokenizers pin, deploy canary -> monitor traces for 30 minutes -> if ok, roll to 20% then full. FastAPI/Starlette patch will follow as P1 after vendor artifacts are in place. Closing thread when all actions done.

jen-sre: Logged canary job and RBAC PR. tagging oncall for merge window.

sec-bot: Vulnerability ticket updated with mitigation steps and assigned owners: sam (tokenizers), carla (compat), maria (kms), jen-sre (rollout).
